correctness.rationale: Exact coordinate overlap factorization gives a constrained product. On each positive-support face, Lagrange stationarity forces positive magnitudes to be equal or complementary; any unequal complementary pair has strictly positive second variation along a sum-of-squares-preserving direction, so cannot maximize. The continuous support-size continuation is unimodal by the explicitly differentiated H, and each adjacent log-ratio rises once then decreases to minus infinity, yielding unique ordered thresholds. Boundary coordinates at 1 give zero product and are excluded because a positive competitor exists for all 0<s<sqrt(d). The standalone finite test printed VERIFY_OK; the analytic proof does not depend on the test.

value.rationale: The radial maximum of the covariogram is a natural fixed-misalignment overlap statistic for a canonical convex body, relevant to geometric matching and autocorrelation. The theorem classifies every optimizer for all dimensions and every admissible distance, proves exactly d-1 distinct geometrically meaningful axis-support transitions and gives their sharp scale and the first exact threshold. It is not a single arbitrary parameter slice or a restatement of the cube overlap product.
